centralClaim: A CNBC analysis of US House disbursement records found that OpenAI's ChatGPT accounted for about 88% of identifiable spending on AI tools by House offices in the year ending 31 March 2026, while the same offices decide how AI is regulated.
sendTest: Le Congrès américain a payé ChatGPT 798 fois en un an, pendant qu'il décide comment encadrer l'IA.

corroboration.quote: The maker of ChatGPT accounted for roughly $9 out of every $10 spent on identifiable AI tools by House offices, committees and institutional accounts during the year ending March 31, according to a CNBC analysis of House disbursement records.

OpenAI's ChatGPT is Congress' AI tool of choice so far in terms of money spent, according to a report from CNBC. OpenAI received roughly 90% of all spending on AI tools by House offices, committees, and institutional accounts during the year ending in March 31, per House disbursement records.

caption:
Le Congrès américain a payé ChatGPT 798 fois en un an, et c'est lui qui écrira les règles de l'IA.

CNBC a analysé les registres de dépenses de la Chambre des représentants. Entre avril 2025 et mars 2026, au moins 113 740 dollars sont partis dans des outils d'IA nommément identifiés. ChatGPT en prend 100 580, soit environ 88 % des dollars et 96 % des transactions. Claude, d'Anthropic, suit à 13 160 dollars.

Le détail qui n'a pas tenu dans la vidéo. Les achats de ChatGPT apparaissent dans au moins 71 bureaux d'élus, environ 1 sur 6. Les bureaux démocrates ont dépensé 54 165 dollars, plus de trois fois les 15 782 dollars des bureaux républicains, alors qu'une partie de ce camp alerte depuis des mois sur les risques de l'IA.

À décharge, ces chiffres sous-estiment l'usage réel. Ils ne comptent ni les comptes gratuits, ni l'IA incluse dans des contrats logiciels plus larges, ni l'essentiel du Sénat.

Un élu qui travaille avec ChatGPT écrit-il de meilleures lois sur l'IA, oui ou non ?

Sources : cnbc.com, techcrunch.com

captionEvidence.quote: CNBC identified at least $113,740 in spending on named AI vendors between April 1, 2025, and March 31, 2026, the most recent data available. ChatGPT accounted for $100,580 of that total across 798 transactions - about 88% of the dollars and 96% of the transactions reviewed. Anthropic's Claude, ChatGPT's closest chatbot rival, was a distant second, totaling $13,160 across 37 transactions.
ChatGPT purchases appeared in at least 71 House member offices - roughly 1 in 6 - while Democratic offices spent more than three times as much as Republican offices on identifiable AI tools.
Democratic member offices accounted for $54,165 in identified AI purchases, more than three times the $15,782 spent by Republican offices.

The numbers underscore an awkward political dynamic: Democrats are leading the visible spending on AI tools, even as many in the party have warned about the technology's risks to workers, privacy, civil rights, elections and corporate power.
The records offer only a partial view of Congress' AI adoption because they exclude free accounts, AI bundled into broader software contracts and most Senate use.

slides.body: Résumer des lois, rédiger des notes, préparer des auditions, et **répondre au courrier des électeurs**.
slides.evidence: Congressional staff are using the tools to summarize legislation, draft memos, prepare hearing materials and respond to constituents - work that can shape how offices understand policy, communicate with voters and manage the flood of information arriving on Capitol Hill.

slides.evidence: OpenAI spent $1 million on federal lobbying in the first quarter of 2026, up 82.5% from the same period a year earlier, according to an analysis by Issue One, a nonprofit government watchdog, of federal lobbying disclosures. Anthropic spent nearly $1.6 million, more than tripling its spending from the first quarter of 2025.
